title: Relationship (1): Stages & Status
instruction: Học về các giai đoạn và trạng thái của một mối quan hệ qua Flashcards.

quizzes.title: Stages & Status
quizzes.instruction: Chọn định nghĩa đúng Tiếng Việt và xem chi tiết ở mặt sau.

front.contextSentence: I've had a crush on her since the first day of high school.

back.mainDefinition: To have a strong but usually temporary feeling of love for someone.
back.mainDefinitionTrans: Cảm nắng, thích thầm ai đó.

wordForms.label: V-ing
wordForms.example: She's having a crush on her new neighbor.

wordForms.label: V2
wordForms.example: He had a crush on his teacher last year.

wordForms.label: V3
wordForms.example: She has had a crush on him for months.

back.example: It's just a teenage crush, it will pass.

detailedDefinitions.example: Many students have a crush on their music teacher.

front.contextSentence: He was flirting with the waitress all evening.

back.mainDefinition: To behave as if sexually attracted to someone, usually in a playful way.
back.mainDefinitionTrans: Tán tỉnh, cưa cẩm ai đó.

wordForms.label: V-ing
wordForms.example: Stop flirting with my sister!

wordForms.label: V2
wordForms.example: He flirted with her at the party.

wordForms.label: V3
wordForms.example: She has flirted with many guys.

back.example: Stop hitting on my best friend!

detailedDefinitions.example: Some people flirt just for fun.
He's a terrible flirt.

front.term: go on a date / date someone
front.contextSentence: Are you dating anyone at the moment?

back.mainDefinition: To go out with someone romantically.
back.mainDefinitionTrans: Đi hẹn hò / Hẹn hò với ai.

wordForms.label: V-ing
wordForms.example: They've been dating for three months.

wordForms.label: V2
wordForms.example: He dated several women before getting married.

wordForms.label: V3
wordForms.example: She has dated many famous people.

back.example: They've been dating for about six months.

synonyms.meaning: gặp gỡ ai đó (theo nghĩa hẹn hò)

detailedDefinitions.example: Would you like to date my friend?
We had a lovely date last night.

front.term: go out with / be seeing someone
front.contextSentence: Is he seeing anyone seriously?

back.mainDefinition: To be in a romantic relationship with someone, often meaning more than just dating.
back.example: I've been going out with him for two years.

detailedDefinitions.example: They are seeing each other exclusively.

collocations.meaning: chỉ hẹn hò với một người

front.contextSentence: She's finally in a relationship after being single for a long time.

back.mainDefinition: To be officially and romantically involved with another person.
back.mainDefinitionTrans: Đang trong một mối quan hệ chính thức.
back.example: They are in a committed relationship.

detailedDefinitions.example: Are you currently in a relationship?

front.contextSentence: Are those two an item now? They're always together.

back.mainDefinition: Two people having a romantic relationship with each other.
back.example: Everyone was surprised when they became an item.

detailedDefinitions.example: Rumors say they're an item now.

front.contextSentence: I think I'm deeply in love with her.

back.mainDefinition: To feel a strong romantic attraction for someone.
back.example: He's head over heels in love.

detailedDefinitions.example: She's truly in love with him.

front.contextSentence: He's completely infatuated with the new girl at the office.

back.mainDefinition: Having a very strong but usually short-lived interest or passion for someone.
back.mainDefinitionTrans: Say mê, si mê (thường thiếu chiều sâu).
back.example: It's not real love; you're just infatuated.

detailedDefinitions.example: He has an infatuated look whenever he sees her.

optionsTrans.text: Si mê, say mê mù quáng

front.contextSentence: They got engaged on Christmas Eve.

back.mainDefinition: Having formally agreed to marry.
back.example: How long have they been engaged?

detailedDefinitions.example: She showed me her engagement ring.

front.contextSentence: They've been married for over 20 years.

back.mainDefinition: Joined in marriage.

wordForms.label: V-ing
wordForms.example: They're getting married next month.

wordForms.label: V2
wordForms.example: They got married in a small ceremony.

wordForms.label: V3
wordForms.example: They have been married for 10 years.

back.example: When did you get married?

detailedDefinitions.example: They plan to marry in the spring.
Are you married or single?

front.contextSentence: They are separated but not yet divorced.

back.mainDefinition: Living apart but not yet legally divorced.
back.example: They've been separated for six months.

detailedDefinitions.example: They're legally separated now.

front.contextSentence: His parents got divorced when he was only five.

back.mainDefinition: No longer married because the marriage has been legally dissolved.
back.example: She is a divorced mother of two.

detailedDefinitions.example: He's been divorced for three years now.

front.contextSentence: They broke up because they wanted different things in life.

back.mainDefinition: To end a romantic relationship.

wordForms.label: V-ing
wordForms.example: I'm thinking about breaking up with him.

wordForms.label: V2
wordForms.example: They broke up last summer.

wordForms.label: V3
wordForms.example: They have broken up several times.

back.example: They split up last month.

detailedDefinitions.example: It's hard to break up with someone you love.

front.contextSentence: Over the years, they just slowly drifted apart.

back.mainDefinition: To gradually become less friendly and eventually end a relationship.
back.mainDefinitionTrans: Dần xa cách, rời xa nhau.
back.example: The couple drifted apart as their interests changed.

detailedDefinitions.example: Many friendships drift apart over time.

front.contextSentence: They managed to patch things up after a long talk.

back.mainDefinition: To restore friendly relations between people.

wordForms.label: V-ing
wordForms.example: They are reconciling after the fight.

wordForms.label: V2
wordForms.example: They reconciled last week.

wordForms.label: V3
wordForms.example: They have reconciled their differences.

back.example: They finally reconciled after the argument.

detailedDefinitions.example: It's time to reconcile with your brother.

front.contextSentence: They've had an on-again, off-again relationship for years.

back.mainDefinition: A relationship that keeps ending and starting again.
back.mainDefinitionTrans: Mối quan hệ lúc có lúc không, không ổn định.
back.example: It's an unstable on-again, off-again romance.

detailedDefinitions.example: Their on-again, off-again relationship is exhausting.

optionsTrans.text: Mối quan hệ tan hợp thất thường

front.contextSentence: They have a purely platonic relationship.

back.mainDefinition: A relationship that is friendly but not romantic or sexual.
back.mainDefinitionTrans: Mối quan hệ thuần túy bạn bè.
back.example: They've been close friends for years in a platonic way.

detailedDefinitions.trans: Quan hệ bạn bè trong sáng
detailedDefinitions.example: A platonic relationship can be very meaningful.

collocations.meaning: tình yêu thuần túy tinh thần

optionsTrans.text: Mối quan hệ bạn bè trong sáng

front.contextSentence: They are just in a casual relationship, nothing serious.

back.mainDefinition: A physical and emotional relationship between two people who may have sex without demanding the extra commitments of a more formal romantic relationship.
back.mainDefinitionTrans: Quan hệ bình thường, không ràng buộc.
back.example: He's not looking for anything more than a casual relationship.

detailedDefinitions.example: Casual relationships are common among young adults.

collocations.meaning: cuộc gặp gỡ không nghiêm túc

front.contextSentence: They've been in a serious relationship for five years.

back.mainDefinition: A committed and long-lasting romantic involvement.
back.mainDefinitionTrans: Mối quan hệ nghiêm túc, lâu dài.
back.example: Are you ready for a long-term relationship?

detailedDefinitions.trans: Quan hệ nghiêm túc dài hạn
detailedDefinitions.example: They're looking for a serious relationship.

front.contextSentence: LDRs can be very challenging but rewarding.

back.mainDefinition: A romantic relationship between two people who live far apart.
back.example: They maintained a long-distance relationship for three years.

synonyms.meaning: quan hệ cách trở địa lý

detailedDefinitions.example: Many couples struggle with long-distance relationships.

front.contextSentence: It took her years to realize she was in a toxic relationship.

back.mainDefinition: A relationship characterized by behaviors that are emotionally or physically damaging.
back.example: Arguments and manipulation are common in toxic relationships.

detailedDefinitions.example: Getting out of a toxic relationship is necessary for mental health.

front.contextSentence: He suffered in an abusive relationship for a long time.

back.mainDefinition: A relationship where one person exerts power and control over another through physical, emotional, or verbal harm.
back.mainDefinitionTrans: Mối quan hệ lạm dụng (tinh thần/thể xác).
back.example: An abusive relationship can leave deep psychological scars.

detailedDefinitions.example: Nobody deserves to be in an abusive relationship.

front.contextSentence: They decided to try an open relationship.

back.mainDefinition: A relationship in which both partners agree that each may have other sexual or romantic partners.
back.example: Open relationships require a lot of communication and trust.

synonyms.meaning: quan hệ không một vợ một chồng

antonyms.meaning: quan hệ một vợ một chồng

detailedDefinitions.example: An open relationship isn't for everyone.

collocations.meaning: không một vợ một chồng có đạo đức

optionsTrans.text: Hôn nhân một vợ một chồng

front.contextSentence: The marriage ended after he had an extramarital affair.

back.mainDefinition: A sexual relationship between a married person and someone who is not their spouse.
back.example: News of the extramarital affair shocked the public.

detailedDefinitions.example: Extramarital affairs often lead to divorce.

front.contextSentence: Their status is a bit of a complicated relationship.

back.mainDefinition: A relationship that is difficult to define or has many problems.
back.example: It's a complicated relationship with many ups and downs.

detailedDefinitions.example: Complicated relationships can be emotionally draining.

collocations.meaning: đời sống tình cảm phức tạp

front.contextSentence: A good relationship is based on mutual understanding.

back.mainDefinition: A situation where two people understand each other's feelings and motives.
back.example: The couple reached a mutual understanding about their finances.

detailedDefinitions.example: Mutual understanding is key to any partnership.

front.contextSentence: I was immediately attracted to her intellect.

back.mainDefinition: To cause someone to have a liking for or interest in something.
back.mainDefinitionTrans: Thu hút / Bị thu hút bởi ai.

wordForms.label: V-ing
wordForms.example: He has a way of attracting people.

wordForms.label: V2
wordForms.example: She attracted many admirers.

wordForms.label: V3
wordForms.example: He has always been attracted to strong women.

back.example: Opposites often attract each other.

detailedDefinitions.example: The new art exhibition attracted many visitors.
I'm physically attracted to him.

front.contextSentence: The holiday was a great chance to bond with the family.

back.mainDefinition: To develop a close connection or strong relationship with someone.
back.mainDefinitionTrans: Gắn kết, tạo sự thân thiết.

wordForms.label: V-ing
wordForms.example: Team building activities are great for bonding.

wordForms.label: V2
wordForms.example: We bonded over our shared experiences.

wordForms.label: V3
wordForms.example: They have bonded deeply over the years.

back.example: They bonded over their shared love of music.

detailedDefinitions.example: Parents bond with their children from birth.
There's a strong bond between the twins.

collocations.meaning: gắn kết qua việc gì đó

front.contextSentence: It takes time to build trust in a relationship.

back.mainDefinition: Belief in the reliability, truth, or ability of someone.
back.example: You have to trust your partner.

detailedDefinitions.example: Trust is the foundation of any good relationship.
I trust you completely.

front.contextSentence: They respect each other's privacy.

back.mainDefinition: A feeling of deep admiration for someone elicited by their qualities or achievements.
back.example: Respect is fundamental to any healthy relationship.

detailedDefinitions.example: We should respect our elders.
He commands respect from his colleagues.

front.contextSentence: My husband was very supportive during my illness.

back.mainDefinition: Providing encouragement or emotional help.
back.example: We support each other through hard times.

detailedDefinitions.example: He supported her decision to go back to school.
She has a very supportive family.

front.contextSentence: I will always cherish the time we spent together.

back.mainDefinition: To protect and care for someone or something lovingly.

wordForms.label: V-ing
wordForms.example: She's cherishing every moment with her newborn.

wordForms.label: V2
wordForms.example: He cherished their friendship deeply.

wordForms.label: V3
wordForms.example: I have always cherished our memories.

back.example: He cherishes his wife dearly.

detailedDefinitions.example: Parents cherish their children's achievements.

front.contextSentence: She adores her grandchildren.

back.mainDefinition: To love and respect someone deeply.

wordForms.label: V-ing
wordForms.example: He has an adoring look in his eyes.

wordForms.label: V2
wordForms.example: She adored her grandmother.

wordForms.label: V3
wordForms.example: He has always adored classical music.

back.example: I absolutely adore him.

detailedDefinitions.example: Children often adore their parents.

front.contextSentence: He deeply cares for his partner's well-being.

back.mainDefinition: The provision of what is necessary for the health, welfare, maintenance, and protection of someone.
back.example: It's clear they care for each other deeply.

detailedDefinitions.example: I really care for you as a friend.

front.contextSentence: They had great chemistry on the first date.

back.mainDefinition: A strong mutual attraction or connection between two people.
back.mainDefinitionTrans: Có sự ăn ý, hợp nhau.
back.example: The actors have amazing chemistry on screen.

detailedDefinitions.example: We had instant chemistry when we met.

collocations.meaning: sự ăn ý ngay lập tức
sự ăn ý không thể phủ nhận

optionsTrans.text: Có sự ăn ý, hợp nhau

front.contextSentence: We are very compatible in our lifestyles.

back.mainDefinition: Able to exist or occur together without conflict.
back.example: They are a highly compatible couple.

detailedDefinitions.example: Their personalities are highly compatible.

collocations.meaning: bài kiểm tra độ tương hợp

front.contextSentence: In any marriage, you have to learn to compromise.

back.mainDefinition: An agreement or a settlement of a dispute that is reached by each side making concessions.

wordForms.label: V-ing
wordForms.example: They are compromising on the wedding plans.

wordForms.label: V2
wordForms.example: We compromised on the price.

wordForms.label: V3
wordForms.example: They have compromised their principles.

back.example: A successful relationship involves healthy compromise.

detailedDefinitions.example: Compromise is essential in any partnership.
I'm willing to compromise on this issue.

front.contextSentence: It's important to communicate effectively about your needs.

back.mainDefinition: To share information or ideas in a clear and successful way.
back.example: Learning to communicate effectively can save a relationship.

detailedDefinitions.example: Couples who communicate effectively have stronger relationships.

front.contextSentence: They share many common interests, like hiking and photography.

back.mainDefinition: To have the same hobbies or things that you enjoy doing.
back.example: Sharing common interests helps keep a relationship strong.

detailedDefinitions.example: Finding someone who shares your interests is wonderful.

front.contextSentence: They aren't ready to make a long-term commitment yet.

back.mainDefinition: A promise to be loyal to someone or something.
back.example: Marriage is a major life commitment.

detailedDefinitions.example: He made a commitment to be more attentive.

front.contextSentence: Loyalty is a very important quality in a friend.

back.mainDefinition: The quality of staying firm in your support for someone.
back.example: She has always been a loyal partner.

detailedDefinitions.example: His loyalty to the company is unquestionable.
Dogs are known to be loyal companions.

collocations.meaning: lòng trung thành không lay chuyển

front.contextSentence: Emotional intimacy is just as important as physical intimacy.

back.mainDefinition: Close familiarity or friendship; closeness.
back.example: They shared a deep sense of intimacy.

detailedDefinitions.example: Intimacy requires vulnerability and trust.

front.contextSentence: He showed his affection by buying her flowers.

back.mainDefinition: A gentle feeling of fondness or liking.
back.example: They have great affection for each other.

detailedDefinitions.example: The mother showed affection to her child.

front.contextSentence: They argue about money all the time.

back.mainDefinition: To give reasons for or against something; to disagree or fight with words.

wordForms.label: V-ing
wordForms.example: Stop arguing about trivial matters.

wordForms.label: V2
wordForms.example: They argued for hours last night.

wordForms.label: V3
wordForms.example: We have argued about this before.

back.example: We had a big argument last night.

detailedDefinitions.example: It's pointless to argue with him.
They had a heated argument.

front.contextSentence: They are always quarreling over small things.

back.mainDefinition: An angry argument or disagreement.
back.example: He had a long-running quarrel with his neighbor.

detailedDefinitions.example: They had a silly quarrel about the TV remote.
The children quarreled over toys.

front.contextSentence: The couple next door are having a row again.

back.mainDefinition: A noisy argument or fight.
back.example: They had a terrible row and didn't speak for days.

synonyms.meaning: cuộc cãi nhau hét vào mặt nhau

detailedDefinitions.example: They had a blazing row about money.

front.contextSentence: There's often a conflict between work and family life.

back.mainDefinition: A serious disagreement or argument.
back.example: They reached a disagreement about the project's direction.

detailedDefinitions.example: There's a conflict of interest here.
His story conflicts with hers.

front.contextSentence: A simple misunderstanding led to a big fight.

back.mainDefinition: A failure to understand something correctly.
back.example: It was just a slight misunderstanding.

detailedDefinitions.example: Let's clear up this misunderstanding.

front.contextSentence: She felt betrayed by her best friend.

back.mainDefinition: To be disloyal to someone who trusts you.
back.example: The betrayal was hard to forgive.

detailedDefinitions.example: He betrayed his country.
This feels like a betrayal of trust.

front.contextSentence: Infidelity is a leading cause of divorce.

back.mainDefinition: Being unfaithful to a spouse or partner.
back.mainDefinitionTrans: Ngoại tình / Sự không chung thủy.
back.example: He admitted to cheating on her.

detailedDefinitions.example: Cheating on your partner is a serious breach of trust.
Marital infidelity destroys relationships.

collocations.meaning: không chung thủy về tình cảm

front.contextSentence: Dishonesty can destroy any relationship.

back.mainDefinition: Lack of honesty or truthfulness.
back.mainDefinitionTrans: Nói dối / Sự không trung thực.
back.example: She couldn't stand his lies.

detailedDefinitions.example: Don't lie to me about what happened.
Dishonesty has no place in a healthy relationship.

front.contextSentence: His jealousy made her uncomfortable.

back.mainDefinition: A feeling of unhappy suspicion, rivalry, or fear of being replaced in another's affection.
back.example: Are you jealous of his success?

detailedDefinitions.example: Jealousy can poison a relationship.
He gets jealous when she talks to other men.

collocations.meaning: con quái vật mắt xanh (thành ngữ chỉ sự ghen tuông)

front.contextSentence: He's very possessive and doesn't like her going out with friends.

back.mainDefinition: Having or showing a desire to control or dominate another person and their interactions.
back.example: A possessive partner can be very controlling.

detailedDefinitions.example: His possessiveness is suffocating.
She has a possessive boyfriend.

front.contextSentence: She felt taken for granted by her husband.

back.mainDefinition: To fail to appreciate someone because they are always there.
back.mainDefinitionTrans: Coi ai đó là hiển nhiên.
back.example: Never take your friends for granted.

detailedDefinitions.example: Don't take your partner's love for granted.

front.contextSentence: Constant neglect led to the end of their marriage.

back.mainDefinition: Fail to care for properly.
back.example: He neglected his duties as a partner.

detailedDefinitions.example: Parents should never neglect their children.
The building shows signs of neglect.

front.contextSentence: Most problems stem from a lack of communication.

back.mainDefinition: A failure to share information or talk about problems.
back.example: Lack of communication can cause major misunderstandings.

detailedDefinitions.example: Their relationship suffered from a lack of communication.

collocations.meaning: sự đổ vỡ trong giao tiếp

front.contextSentence: As they got older, they just seemed to grow apart.

back.mainDefinition: To gradually become less friendly or interested in each other.
back.example: They grew apart after years of different paths.

detailedDefinitions.example: Many childhood friends grow apart as adults.

collocations.meaning: cảm thấy như đang xa cách

front.contextSentence: It's sad when couples fall out of love.

back.mainDefinition: To stop having romantic feelings for someone.
back.mainDefinitionTrans: Hết yêu, không còn tình cảm.
back.example: She felt she had fallen out of love with him.

detailedDefinitions.example: Sometimes people just fall out of love.

collocations.phrase: realize you've fallen out of love
collocations.meaning: nhận ra mình đã hết yêu

front.contextSentence: Resentment can poison a relationship over time.

back.mainDefinition: A feeling of deep and bitter anger and ill-will.
back.example: She felt a lot of resentment towards her ex.

detailedDefinitions.example: Years of resentment built up between them.

front.contextSentence: He was absolutely heartbroken after the breakup.

back.mainDefinition: Feeling extremely sad or crushed because of a lost love.
back.example: It takes time to heal a heartbreak.

detailedDefinitions.example: She was heartbroken when he left.
First heartbreak is often the hardest.

collocations.meaning: khách sạn của những trái tim tan vỡ

front.contextSentence: It was very considerate of you to bring me flowers.

back.mainDefinition: Careful not to cause inconvenience or hurt to others.
back.mainDefinitionTrans: Chu đáo, ân cần, biết nghĩ cho người khác.
back.example: He's always very considerate towards his neighbors.

detailedDefinitions.example: A considerate gesture like holding the door open.

front.contextSentence: She's very manipulative and always gets her own way.

back.mainDefinition: Characterized by unscrupulous control of a situation or person.
back.mainDefinitionTrans: Có tính thao túng, hay điều khiển người khác.
back.example: A manipulative person uses your emotions against you.

detailedDefinitions.example: Manipulative behavior in relationships is toxic.

front.contextSentence: He's very thoughtful and always remembers my birthday.

back.mainDefinition: Showing consideration for the needs of other people.
back.example: It was thoughtful of you to call.

detailedDefinitions.example: A thoughtful gift shows you care.

front.contextSentence: She has a very caring nature.

back.mainDefinition: Displaying kindness and concern for others.
back.example: He's a caring father.

detailedDefinitions.example: A caring attitude makes a big difference.

front.contextSentence: He's very affectionate with his children.

back.mainDefinition: Readily showing fondness or tenderness.
back.mainDefinitionTrans: Hay thể hiện tình cảm, âu yếm.
back.example: She gave him an affectionate hug.

detailedDefinitions.trans: Âu yếm, thể hiện tình cảm
detailedDefinitions.example: Affectionate couples often hold hands.

collocations.meaning: người hay thể hiện tình cảm

optionsTrans.text: Âu yếm, thể hiện tình cảm

front.contextSentence: You can always count on him; he's very dependable.

back.mainDefinition: Trustworthy and reliable.
back.example: A dependable friend is there when you need them.

detailedDefinitions.example: She's the most dependable employee we have.

front.contextSentence: He's too self-centered to think about others' feelings.

back.mainDefinition: Preoccupied with oneself and one's own affairs.
back.mainDefinitionTrans: Ích kỷ, chỉ nghĩ đến bản thân.
back.example: A selfish person puts their own needs first.

synonyms.meaning: tự cho mình là trung tâm

detailedDefinitions.example: Self-centered behavior can damage relationships.

optionsTrans.text: Ích kỷ, chỉ nghĩ đến mình

front.contextSentence: It was inconsiderate of him to be so late.

back.mainDefinition: Thoughtlessly causing hurt or inconvenience to others.
back.example: Inconsiderate behavior shows lack of respect.

detailedDefinitions.example: Playing loud music late at night is inconsiderate.

front.term: fall head over heels in love
front.contextSentence: He fell head over heels in love with her the moment they met.

back.mainDefinition: To fall deeply and suddenly in love with someone.
back.mainDefinitionTrans: Yêu say đắm, yêu cuồng nhiệt.
back.example: They are perfectly head over heels in love.

detailedDefinitions.example: Completely head over heels for someone.

front.contextSentence: They are finally tying the knot this summer after a long engagement.

back.mainDefinition: To get married.
back.example: So when are you two going to tie the knot?

detailedDefinitions.example: They tied the knot in Vegas.

front.contextSentence: He's planning to pop the question on their anniversary.

back.mainDefinition: To propose marriage.
back.example: He finally popped the question last night.

detailedDefinitions.example: He popped the question at the Eiffel Tower.

collocations.phrase: right time to pop the question
collocations.meaning: thời điểm thích hợp để cầu hôn

front.contextSentence: They want to settle down and start a family.

back.mainDefinition: To establish a stable life in one place, especially by marrying.
back.mainDefinitionTrans: Ổn định cuộc sống (thường sau khi lập gia đình).
back.example: It's time to settle down and have kids.

detailedDefinitions.example: After traveling, he's ready to settle down.

front.contextSentence: Every relationship has its ups and downs.

back.mainDefinition: To experience both good and bad periods.
back.example: Marriage has its ups and downs.

detailedDefinitions.example: We've had our ups and downs, but we're still together.

front.contextSentence: They decided to work through their problems instead of breaking up.

back.mainDefinition: To resolve difficulties by discussing and dealing with them.
back.mainDefinitionTrans: Cùng nhau vượt qua khó khăn.
back.example: Counseling helps couples work through their issues.

detailedDefinitions.example: It takes effort to work through relationship problems.

optionsTrans.text: Cùng nhau vượt qua khó khăn

front.contextSentence: She gave him the cold shoulder after their argument.

back.mainDefinition: To deliberately ignore someone or treat them in an unfriendly way.
back.mainDefinitionTrans: Thờ ơ, lạnh nhạt với ai.
back.example: He's been giving me the cold shoulder all week.

detailedDefinitions.example: Getting the cold shoulder hurts.

optionsTrans.text: Thờ ơ, lạnh nhạt với ai

front.contextSentence: We need to have a heart-to-heart talk about our future.

back.mainDefinition: To have a sincere and intimate conversation.
back.mainDefinitionTrans: Nói chuyện chân tình, cởi mở.
back.example: After our heart-to-heart, I felt much better.

detailedDefinitions.example: A heart-to-heart can solve many misunderstandings.

collocations.meaning: có cuộc nói chuyện chân tình

optionsTrans.text: Nói chuyện chân tình, cởi mở

front.contextSentence: I get along very well with my mother-in-law.

back.mainDefinition: To have a harmonious or friendly relationship.
back.example: Do you get along with your colleagues?

detailedDefinitions.example: They just don't get along.

front.contextSentence: I don't know how she puts up with his constant complaining.

back.mainDefinition: To tolerate or endure something or someone unpleasant.
back.mainDefinitionTrans: Chịu đựng ai đó/điều gì đó.
back.example: She put up with his bad temper for years.

detailedDefinitions.example: I can't put up with it anymore.

front.contextSentence: I didn't like him at first, but he's grown on me.

back.mainDefinition: To become more liked or enjoyable over time.
back.mainDefinitionTrans: Dần trở nên thích ai/điều gì.
back.example: This song grows on you after a few listens.

detailedDefinitions.example: He's the kind of person who grows on you.

front.contextSentence: I think he has feelings for her.

back.mainDefinition: To have romantic feelings towards someone.
back.example: She admitted she has feelings for her best friend.

detailedDefinitions.example: Having feelings for someone can be confusing.

front.contextSentence: It took me a year to be over my ex.

back.mainDefinition: To have recovered from a past romantic relationship.
back.example: She says she's completely over him now.

detailedDefinitions.example: Being over someone takes time.

front.contextSentence: He led her on by saying he loved her.

back.mainDefinition: To make someone believe something that is not true, especially about your feelings.
back.mainDefinitionTrans: Làm cho ai hiểu lầm về tình cảm của mình.
back.example: Don't lead him on if you're not interested.

detailedDefinitions.example: Leading someone on is cruel.

optionsTrans.text: Làm ai hiểu lầm về tình cảm

front.contextSentence: After five years, they decided to call it quits.

back.mainDefinition: To end a relationship or stop doing something.
back.example: It's time to call it quits on this project.

detailedDefinitions.example: Sometimes it's best to call it quits.

collocations.phrase: call it quits on a relationship

front.contextSentence: They're working on their marriage with a counselor.

back.mainDefinition: To make efforts to improve or repair a relationship.
back.mainDefinitionTrans: Cố gắng vun đắp cho mối quan hệ.
back.example: You have to work on a relationship to keep it healthy.

detailedDefinitions.example: Working on communication helps relationships.

optionsTrans.text: Cố gắng vun đắp mối quan hệ
